expect.note: The value /version serves is one the build DERIVED for itself, and the mechanism is graded, not the route (the route is `version-never-guesses-a-build-sha`'s job and its 13 probes are untouched). Four conjuncts: .dockerignore admits `.git` into the build context; the Dockerfile declares no `ARG ZEABUR_GIT_COMMIT_SHA` (the 2026-08-28 live read proved the platform never fills it, so the only feeder left was a hand-typed dashboard build-arg value that every later build would re-bake -- ADR-033 Decision 2's rejected path at build time, PR #65 R3); the derivation RUN line, extracted by regex and EXECUTED with substituted paths, writes this checkout's HEAD when pointed at the repo root and exits 0 leaving an EMPTY file when pointed at a git-less directory -- empty being exactly what /version answers `unavailable` for; and `.git` never reaches the final image -- the derivation lives in an earlier stage on the same base tag and the final stage COPYs exactly one file back out of it. Both COPY conjuncts are graded on the SOURCE, not the destination, through one normaliser (flags stripped, trailing `/` off, `ADD` read like `COPY`): the derive stage must copy the whole context (`.`) or `.git` itself, and every final-stage source must be ON A FOUR-ENTRY ALLOWLIST of what this image ships -- `src/browser/requirements.txt`, `src`, `docs/support-matrix.md`, `/BUILD_SHA` -- with no exemption for `--from=`, since the derive stage holds the whole context at `/ctx`. Set membership, not a hunt for sources that look dangerous (PR #67 R6/R7/R8). Every bypass and every correct spelling is exercised by mutations the check runs itself, in both directions -- including the parser's own surface (case, indentation, line continuation), since a line the parser fails to match contributes no source and so cannot be refused by an allowlist (PR #67 R10).

provenance:
M44-P1 remedy phase, written before the Dockerfile changed. ADR-033 deliberately left one fact unverified -- whether Zeabur passes its Git-group variables to a Dockerfile build -- and designed the route to fail to the honest null if not. The first deploy after PR #65's merge (6089850) settled it, on 2026-08-28: `curl https://whaleforce-browser-agent.zeabur.app/version` answered {"sha":null,"source":"unavailable"} while /healthz was ok, so the new build IS running and the ARG is never filled. ADR-033 Consequences pre-recorded exactly this outcome and its sole remedy: a sha the build derives for itself. ADR-034 is the ruling; this case is its mechanism guard.

RED, watched, against the pre-remedy tree (the merged PR #65 Dockerfile and .dockerignore, unmodified): 4 of the check's conjunct keys fired at once -- dockerignore_excludes_git ['.git'], build_arg_still_declared ['ARG ZEABUR_GIT_COMMIT_SHA=""'], single_stage ('1 FROM line(s)'), derive_command_missing. The two executed probes could not fire on that tree (no derive command to extract), which is why the shape conjuncts exist separately: a red that only said 'command missing' would go green on any RUN line shaped right, executed or not.

The fail-to-empty probe was then mutation-tested on a scratch copy of the FIXED Dockerfile, because an executed probe never seen red proves nothing (rule 2): with the `|| : > /BUILD_SHA` fallback deleted from the derive RUN line, the extraction still matches (the fallback group is optional in the regex ON PURPOSE, so a fallback-less variant is extracted and executed rather than reported as a shape miss) and `gitless-context-empty-file` went red with exit 128 -- `git rev-parse` failing in a directory with no repository and nothing catching it, the exact build behaviour that would break a deploy whose context lacks `.git` instead of publishing the honest `unavailable`. A second mutation, deriving from a directory the stage never COPYs into (`-C /nowhere`), was predicted to redden the executed head probe and instead went red one conjunct earlier, on `derive_stage_never_copies_the_context` -- recorded as it happened, not as predicted: the shape conjunct fires first because an un-COPY'd context is visible statically, and what that red demonstrates is THAT conjunct's non-vacuity. The `derives-this-checkouts-head` probe itself has no reachable in-shape Dockerfile mutation today (the extraction regex admits essentially one command); what it executes against every run is the extraction-and-substitution machinery, and its declared job is to catch a future widening of that regex admitting a command that does not produce HEAD -- the triage note carries this as a ceiling.

Worktree caveat, recorded because this repo works in them: the derivation copies the CONTEXT's `.git`, and in a git worktree that is a pointer file into a repository the copy does not include, so a docker build FROM A WORKTREE would produce the honest empty file. The executed probes are immune -- they point the extracted command at the live checkout, where git follows the pointer -- which is also why `derives-this-checkouts-head` holds in the CI checkout and in this worktree alike.

PR #67 round 1 found both COPY conjuncts vacuous in the direction they are named for, and both are now graded through mutations the check executes against a scratch Dockerfile rather than through prose. R1: the derive stage's COPY was matched on its DESTINATION, so `COPY . /ctx` -> `COPY src /ctx` -- a subtree that cannot contain `.git` -- returned {'passed': True, 'wrong': {}} while the real build would derive nothing and /version would be `unavailable` forever. R2: `.dockerignore` used to filter `.git` out of every stage, so a whole-context COPY into the final image was harmless; this change is what makes it reachable, and `COPY src/ /app/src/` -> `COPY . /app/` shipped the entire git history into a publicly deployed image past a substring scan for `.git` that such a line never contains -- also {'passed': True, 'wrong': {}}. Both mutations were re-run here before the guards were written (green, reproducing the reviewer), then the two mutation rows were added and WATCHED RED against the round-1 guards -- {'mutation_derive-stage-copies-a-subtree_not_caught': ..., 'mutation_final-stage-copies-the-context_not_caught': ...} -- and only then were the guards fixed. They now report {'derive_stage_never_copies_the_context': {'context': '/ctx', 'copies': 'src', ...}} and {'final_stage_copies_git': ['COPY . /app/']}. Each mutation asserts its own substitution happened, so a rename that made the pattern absent is a loud `mutation_..._is_vacuous` rather than a row quietly passing on an unmutated copy.

PR #67 round 2 replaced the mechanism rather than widening it, on the reviewer's ruling. The round-1 repair was a denylist and it failed in BOTH directions at once, which is the signature this repo already acted on at PR #65 R5/R8 when it retired a phrase denylist for asking a regex a semantic question. It failed OPEN on five spellings of the same property -- `COPY ./ /app/`, `ADD . /app/`, `COPY --chown=pwuser . /app/`, `COPY --link . /app/` (R7) and `COPY --from=build-identity /ctx/.git /app/.git` (R6, a COVERAGE REGRESSION: the pre-round-1 substring scan caught that one, and the repair's `--from=` exemption rested on a comment that was false for this Dockerfile -- `build-identity` holds the whole context at `/ctx`) -- and CLOSED on `COPY ./ /ctx` and `COPY --link . /ctx`, reddening a correct Dockerfile (R8).

The final-stage rule is now set membership against the four things this image ships, so a spelling Docker has not invented yet is red by default instead of green by default. One normaliser serves both conjuncts, which is what closed R8 with no separate fix, and the derive-stage conjunct now reads EVERY COPY into the context rather than the first.

Verified by execution, not by reasoning, in three directions. (a) All six bypasses red on the right conjunct, each as a self-test row the check runs on every invocation. (b) The four correct spellings green: `COPY ./ /ctx`, `COPY --link . /ctx`, `COPY .git /ctx/.git`, and a derive stage with two COPY lines into the context. (c) Against the guard it replaced -- the reviewer's own instruction, since R6's lesson was a repair losing coverage: swept seven `.git` lines through both the retired `re.search(r'(?m)^COPY\s+[^\n]*\.git', final_text)` and the new rule. Five agree, one is newly caught (`ADD .git /app/.git`, which the old scan missed because it named one instruction), and exactly one diverges the other way -- `COPY src/ /app/.git`, an ALLOWED source copied to a destination merely named `.git`, red under the old scan and green here. That is the old scan's over-fire and not lost coverage: git history can only reach the image through a SOURCE, and no allowlisted source is a repository. Recorded rather than engineered away, and the divergence is one line either way.

PR #67 round 3 found the allowlist correct and the PARSER under it not. Docker keywords are case-insensitive and may be indented, and the shared instruction regex was anchored to `^(?:COPY|ADD)` case-sensitively at column 0 -- so a line it failed to match contributed no source and therefore could not be unlisted: default-red for lines it parsed, default-GREEN for every line it did not, which is the fail-open-and-fail-closed signature that retired the denylist one round earlier, arriving one layer down. Reproduced on 6373427 before the fix, both directions: `copy . /app/`, `Copy . /app/`, `add . /app/`, ` COPY . /app/` and a tab-indented COPY all shipped the whole context and stayed GREEN, while `copy . /ctx` and ` COPY . /ctx` falsely REDDENED a correct derive stage. Fixed with one regex on the shared parser -- `(?mi)^[ \t]*(?:COPY|ADD)\s+` -- so both conjuncts move together, and line continuations are joined first, a sixth spelling found while fixing rather than reported (`COPY \` + newline + `. /app/` was green too). All eight were watched RED as self-test rows before the regex changed.

R11, same round: the row list held TEN rows while two documents claimed ELEVEN, and the absent one was the row guarding the half of R8 the round-2 artifact called fixed -- that the derive conjunct reads EVERY COPY into the context rather than the first. It is added, and watched red the only way it can be: against a first-match-only read of the same parser, where `COPY src /ctx` followed by `COPY . /ctx` reports `derive_stage_never_copies_the_context` with `copies: ['src']`. The count is now a constant the check reads back against its own loop, so no document can state a number the list does not hold.

triage.note:
Pure code plus two subprocess runs of the Dockerfile's own derive command; no browser, no network, no spend -- what `invariant` admits. `invariant`-only for ADR-033 Decision 4's reason unchanged: the `fast` band has no room and this case does not need the app at all.

Declared ceilings, in the sibling case's spirit. (1) The two textual conjuncts are scans: a new spelling of the `.git` exclusion (`.git*`, a glob, an exclusion in a nested ignore file) or of the ARG (a renamed build argument fed to the same file) is invisible; the backstop is the post-merge live read M44-P1's block requires, where a stripped or re-excluded `.git` reads `unavailable`. (2) The executed probes run the extracted command under `sh` on THIS machine -- no Docker exists here (declared in ADR-034 as in ADR-033), so what is proven is the command's behaviour, not the image's: a base image lacking `git` would fall to the `|| :` branch and publish `unavailable`, which the design accepts and the probes cannot distinguish from a platform that strips `.git`. (3) The regex admits one command shape; a semantically equivalent derive line spelled differently (a heredoc, a script COPY'd in) is `derive_command_missing` -- red, loudly, so the failure mode is a false alarm demanding the regex widen, never a silent pass. The flip side, declared: because the shape is that tight, `derives-this-checkouts-head` currently has no reachable in-shape mutation to redden it -- it exercises the extraction/substitution machinery on every run and earns its keep the day the regex is widened. (4) The stage checks are line-anchored regexes over the Dockerfile text. A `COPY` split across a line continuation used to be invisible and is not any more -- continuations are joined before the scan and the case is a self-test row (PR #67 R10) -- and the other instruction regexes are still case-sensitive at column 0, which does NOT fail closed uniformly -- an earlier version of this sentence said it did, and PR #67 R13/R14 falsified it in both halves. What was actually observed, each re-run at round 4: lowercasing BOTH `FROM` lines reports `single_stage` (that is the spelling round 3 probed, and the sentence generalised it to `a lowercase FROM`); lowercasing only the DERIVE stage's `FROM` raises an uncaught `ValueError: max() iterable argument is empty` from the stage-index lookup, which the runner turns into a case ERROR -- loud, so the gate still stops, but the named conjunct never reports and no document should have said it did; and `arg ZEABUR_GIT_COMMIT_SHA=""` in lowercase passes GREEN, so the ARG regex fails OPEN. The retracted claim was `loud and wrong, never quiet and wrong`; the ARG case is quiet and wrong. Left as-is deliberately -- see ceiling (9): more spellings is the surface this case stopped chasing. (5) The executed probes need a resolvable HEAD, so a `container:` CI job, a `git archive` tarball or an installed copy reddens a suite gated at 100% with a correct Dockerfile -- the same ceiling `version-never-guesses-a-build-sha` declares, and the same debt: `M44-P1-D2` names both functions (PR #67 R5). (6) The final-stage rule is an ALLOWLIST, and the tradeoff is deliberate: a legitimate new final-stage COPY is red until someone adds its source to the four-entry list. That is a false red in the SAFE direction -- it fails closed and costs one deliberate edit -- and it is what makes a COPY/ADD spelling nobody here has written refused rather than admitted, after two rounds of denylist failed open and closed at once (PR #67 R6/R7/R8). What that does NOT reach is stated in ceiling (9): the allowlist can only refuse sources the PARSER hands it. (7) What the allowlist does NOT read is the destination: `COPY src/ /app/.git` copies an allowed source into a directory merely named `.git` and is green, where the retired substring scan was red. Verified rather than assumed, and it is the one divergence in a twelve-line sweep re-run at round 3, where the other six divergences all run the other way (`ADD`, lowercase, indented and continued `.git` COPYs the retired scan missed); git history can only reach the image through a source. (8) TWENTY self-test rows -- 13 that must be red on a named conjunct, 6 that must stay clean, and the vacuity guard itself, which is a row because it was the one piece of the exercise set nothing exercised. The count lives in `_BUILD_SHA_SELF_TEST_ROWS` and the check reads it back against the loop, because two documents said ELEVEN while the loop held TEN and the missing row guarded a property a resolution artifact called fixed (PR #67 R11). A row whose target string is renamed out of the Dockerfile reports `mutation_..._is_vacuous` rather than passing on an unmutated copy. (9) THE BOUNDARY, named rather than implied: this is a text scan of `COPY`/`ADD` instructions, and it cannot see an instruction that ships the tree without one. Verified, not reasoned: `RUN --mount=type=bind,source=.git,target=/tmp/g cp -r /tmp/g /app/.git` is GREEN here and puts the whole history in the image. `ARG`-substituted sources and heredoc forms were probed in the same pass and both fail closed; the lowercase-`FROM` and lowercase-`arg` results are in ceiling (4) and are NOT both fail-closed. That is one of THREE demonstrated evasion classes, and the third is the reason this stops here: instruction SPELLING (round 3 -- case, indentation, continuation; pinned red now), instruction CLASS (the `RUN --mount` above, which no COPY/ADD scan can see), and PARSER level -- a comment line ending in a backslash swallows the next instruction, so `# x \` + newline + `COPY . /app/` parses to `[]` and ships the whole context GREEN, where the retired substring regex caught it. That third class was INTRODUCED by round 3's own repair: joining continuations is what closed the R10 spelling hole, and Docker strips comments before joining, which this parser does not. Three rounds, three classes, each deeper than the last and the newest one manufactured by the previous fix -- a surface that grows as fast as it is covered. The disposition is ADR-034's: the guarantee a text scan can carry is bounded, the honest upgrade is a CI job that builds the image and asserts `/app/.git` does not exist, and until that exists the bypass is named here and in the ADR rather than chased one instruction at a time. Same restore discipline as the sibling: nothing global is mutated -- the check writes only under tempfile.TemporaryDirectory and touches no module attribute, no environment variable.
